```suggestion

```
This comment can be removed as its implicitly understood.
If these parameters are never modified, do pass them as constants
You may need to add test cases for `encode_update_security_revision_req()` API as well.
I prefer this mentions the short spec name as well, so: `dsp: firmware_update: Added ...`
Please use imperative mode here too, so `dsp: firmware_update: Add ...` rather than `dsp: Added ...`

This mostly duplicates the patch subject. I suggest just adding the spec ID and version to the patch subject, then removing this line:


```
dsp: firmware_update: Add Update Security Revision from DSP0267 v1.3.0
```
Can you please re-wrap this to 72 characters?
Hi Mayank, thanks for the change. I have some comments inline.
Make this match the patch subject (see discussion on commit message)
The general preference is that we add `PLDM_FWUP_` as a symbol prefix to identify where it's coming from. Can you please do so here?

I appreciate you're fixing a typo, however, this should be done by adding the new enum member with the correct spelling, and leaving the misspelled member in place until we've tagged a release with the corrected member.

Please avoid abbreviating member names for messages. The abbreviations make it trickier to trace them back to the spec.

Please fix throughout.

I understand you're probably aiming for consistency with existing structs here, however, I ask that we don't add further `__attribute__((packed))` structs going forward:


https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/799fba23bb28bf4f7b500c030313aeacdb3c53ce/CONTRIBUTING.md#L315-L316

Please fix throughout.
In the case where the only response is a completion code I'm okay with accepting a `uint8_t *` parameter to the decode API rather than force you to define a struct.

Please don't return PLDM completion codes from encode/decode APIs. Instead, return 0 on success, or a negative errno value on failure:


https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/799fba23bb28bf4f7b500c030313aeacdb3c53ce/CONTRIBUTING.md#L361-L364

Please fix throughout.

Please don't decompose messages into individual members:

https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/799fba23bb28bf4f7b500c030313aeacdb3c53ce/CONTRIBUTING.md#L306-L310

Please make sure your additions follow the ABI lifecycle:


https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#library-background

This must be `LIBPLDM_ABI_TESTING` for now.

Please rewrite using the msgbuf APIs.

Please fix throughout.

Please guard tests for APIs in the "testing" category with:

```
#ifdef LIBPLDM_API_TESTING
TEST(...)
{
    ...
}
#endif
```


The guard should be placed around each individual test.

Please fix throughout.

This needs to be replaced with `PLDM_MSG_DEFINE_P()` from `include/libpldm/base.h`.

Please fix throughout.

The NOLINT should be a hint that this isn't desirable. Existing instances are historical and not a reflection of current expectations.
Generally yhou should use `ASSERT_EQ()` in this case to prevent subsequent `EXPECT_*()` invocations from spuriously failing on unexpected errors.
Can you please define this immediately underneath your addition of the struct below? I recognise this isn't consistent through the file, but it will be helpful in the long run.
This needs to be a pointer, in-out parameter

All return codes need to be negative errno values. This specific instance should be `return -EINVAL;`

Please fix throughout.
Make this `sizeof(*completion_code)` and lines 3307-3309 become unnecessary.
Hi Mayank - I caught a missed errno conversion in the implementation, but then also spotted some naming concerns. Sorry for going around on this a bit 😞
Ah! Sorry, should have caught this earlier, but the prefix for the struct should be `pldm_fwup` as well, so `pldm_fwup_update_security_revision_req`.

... and likewise, this should match the struct name. Sorry for not catching that earlier.

```
int encode_pldm_fwup_update_security_revision_req(...);
```
